title_en: The Martyrdom of Conon the Gardener
author: Acts of the Martyrs
occasion: After Papias, Diodorus and Claudian were completed as martyrs, the governor came to Magydus and tried through a herald to summon the inhabitants. The inhabitants fled, leaving the city empty, and he sent searchers to look everywhere and house by house.
argument: The inhabitants of Magydus flee, leaving the city empty, and the governor's searchers find only the old gardener Conon watering the imperial garden at Carmena. Bound to a horse and dragged in, Conon is presented by Naodorus as obedient to the gods, laws and emperor, and Conon corrects Naodorus's presentation with Not as you say it is, affirming he obeys Christ the great King. Asked about home, kindred and name, he declares himself from Nazareth of Galilee and a kinsman and ancestral worshipper of Christ above all gods. The governor demands as the sole requirement only a small amount of incense, wine and a branch with the cry Highest, save this multitude, and says he learned exactly from Jews about Christ's people, deeds and crucified death, and that they produced Christ's hypomnemata and read them to him. Conon denounces lifeless stones and human handiwork, refuses to sacrifice, and warns the governor of divine judgment in Tartarus and unquenchable fire; nailed under the joints of his feet, he is forced to run before the chariot under two whips while singing, then kneels at the marketplace, commends his soul to Jesus, and dies as an offering to God.

outline.move: The governor sits in the suburb of Zeus at Magydus, summons the residents by herald, finds city and fields deserted, and sends searchers.
The city-father Naodorus called Apelles and the assistant Origen with guards find Conon watering the imperial garden at Carmena, greet and summon him, then bind him to a horse to be dragged.

Naodorus presents Conon to the governor as obedient to gods, laws and emperor, Conon corrects Naodorus's characterization that he obeys Christ the great King, and Origen reports that only this old man was found.
The governor asks Conon's home, family and name, and Conon answers that he is from Nazareth of Galilee and kin to Christ, whom he worships above all gods.

The governor demands only token incense, wine, branch and acclamation, disparages Christ as a crucified man known from what Jews told and read to him, Conon denounces idols as sightless stones and refuses, and warns of the judge, Tartarus and unquenchable fire against threats of lion, sea-beasts, cross and burning cauldron.

After counsel the governor puts nails under the joints and nails Conon's feet and makes him run before his chariot while driven by two whips and singing a psalm, Conon prays to Jesus at the marketplace and gives up his spirit, and the governor retreats while the narrator closes with doxology.

cast.name: Conon

cast.name: The governor

cast.name: Naodorus, also called Apelles

cast.name: Papias
cast.who: Christian martyr completed just before Conon.

cast.name: Diodorus
cast.who: Christian martyr completed with Papias and Claudian.

cast.name: Claudian
cast.who: Christian martyr completed with Papias and Diodorus.

cast.name: Jesus Christ
cast.who: Confessed by Conon as great King, God over all, Saviour and Lord.

perform a pagan offering to win release

scripture: The author quotes the Greek Old Testament without giving book titles; psalm language follows the LXX numbering, about one number lower than modern Hebrew/English psalm numbers. Cite the single psalm quotation Ὑπομένων ὑπέμεινα τὸν κύριον as Ps 40:1 modern (LXX Ps 39:2), and cite the worm-and-fire warning as Isa 66:24, also known from Mark 9:48, giving both LXX and modern references.
uncertain: Date of composition and of the persecution setting: no emperor, governor, or year is named, only an order of the emperor.
Identity of the governor, the exact force of city-father, assistant, keeper of order and other titles, and topography of Magydus, the suburb of Zeus, and Carmena.
Why Origen addresses Conon as Papia in section 2: whether nickname, mistake, confusion with the martyr Papias, or textual corruption.
Whether the psalm verse and worm/fire saying are deliberate quotations with a fixed text or general scriptural language, and which psalm-number system readers should print.

_unresolved_facts.claim: The inhabitants fled, leaving the city empty
_unresolved_facts.source_quote: ὥστε τὴν πόλιν μόνην ὑπολειφθῆναι μετὰ τοῦ μιαροῦ ἄρχοντος καὶ τῆς τάξεως αὐτοῦ
_unresolved_facts.fix: The inhabitants fled, leaving the city with only the foul governor and his staff/garrison remaining

_unresolved_facts.claim: Bound to a horse and dragged in
_unresolved_facts.source_quote: κελεύει δεθῆναι αὐτὸν τῷ ἵππῳ αὐτοῦ καὶ οὕτως ἕλκεσθαι
_unresolved_facts.fix: Bound to Naodorus's horse and dragged (not simply 'a horse'—it is specifically Naodorus's horse)

_unresolved_facts.claim: Conon corrects Naodorus's presentation with Not as you say it is, affirming he obeys Christ the great King
_unresolved_facts.source_quote: Οὐχ ὡς ἔστιν λέγεις· ἐγὼ γὰρ πείθομαι τῷ μεγάλῳ βασιλεῖ Χριστῷ
_unresolved_facts.fix: Conon corrects Naodorus with 'Not as it is do you speak' (οὐχ ὡς ἔστιν λέγεις), affirming he obeys Christ the great King

_unresolved_facts.claim: The governor demands as the sole requirement only a small amount of incense, wine and a branch with the cry Highest, save this multitude
_unresolved_facts.source_quote: Οὐ λέγω σοι θῦσον, ἀλλ᾽ οὐδέ τι τῶν τοιούτων ποίησον. Μόνον δὲ λάβε λίβανον βραχὺν καὶ οἶνον καὶ θαλλὸν καὶ εἰπέ· Ὕψιστε, σῶσε τὸ πλῆθος τοῦτο. Τοῦτο εἰπέ, καὶ ἕτερον οὐδέν σε ἐπάγω
_unresolved_facts.fix: The governor says he does not demand sacrifice, only that Conon take a little incense, wine and a branch and say 'Highest, save this multitude'—saying this and nothing else will be required

_unresolved_facts.claim: and says he learned exactly from Jews about Christ's people, deeds and crucified death, and that they produced Christ's hypomnemata and read them to him
_unresolved_facts.source_quote: Ὡς ἔμαθον παρὰ Ἰουδαίων ἀκριβῶς, καὶ τί τὸ γένος αὐτοῦ καὶ ὅσα ἐνεδείξατο τῷ ἔθνει αὐτῶν καὶ πῶς ἀπέθανεν σταυρωθείς. Προκομίσαντες γὰρ αὐτοῦ τὰ ὑπομνήματα ἐπανέγνωσάν μοι
_unresolved_facts.fix: and says he learned exactly from Jews Christ's family/race, what he displayed to their nation, and how he died crucified; for producing his hypomnemata they read them back to him

_unresolved_facts.claim: The governor sits in the suburb of Zeus at Magydus
_unresolved_facts.source_quote: ἐπεβέβηκεν ὁ ἡγεμὼν τῇ πόλει Μαγυδῷ, καὶ καθίσας ἐν τῷ προαστείῳ τοῦ Διὸς
_unresolved_facts.fix: The governor came to the city of Magydus and sat in the suburb of Zeus

_unresolved_facts.claim: the city-father Naodorus called Apelles and the assistant Origen with guards find Conon
_unresolved_facts.source_quote: Καί τις βοηθὸς ὀνόματι Ὠριγένης, ἐπιβὰς καὶ αὐτὸς σὺν τῷ προειρημένῳ Ναοδώρῳ μετὰ καὶ εἰρηναρχικῆς τάξεως καὶ ἑτέρων τινῶν
_unresolved_facts.fix: Naodorus called Apelles, a city-father, and another person, a neōkoros, requested help; the assistant Origen, mounting up with the aforementioned Naodorus along with a peace-officer unit and certain others, find Conon

_unresolved_facts.claim: Conon corrects Naodorus's characterization that he obeys Christ the great King
_unresolved_facts.source_quote: Οὐχ ὡς ἔστιν λέγεις· ἐγὼ γὰρ πείθομαι τῷ μεγάλῳ βασιλεῖ Χριστῷ
_unresolved_facts.fix: Conon corrects Naodorus with 'Not as it is do you speak; for I obey the great King Christ'

_unresolved_facts.claim: The governor demands only token incense, wine, branch and acclamation
_unresolved_facts.source_quote: Οὐ λέγω σοι θῦσον, ἀλλ᾽ οὐδέ τι τῶν τοιούτων ποίησον. Μόνον δὲ λάβε λίβανον βραχὺν καὶ οἶνον καὶ θαλλὸν καὶ εἰπέ· Ὕψιστε, σῶσε τὸ πλῆθος τοῦτο
_unresolved_facts.fix: The governor says he does not demand sacrifice, only that Conon take a little incense, wine and branch and say 'Highest, save this multitude'

_unresolved_facts.claim: disparages Christ as a crucified man known from what Jews told and read to him
_unresolved_facts.source_quote: Ὡς ἔμαθον παρὰ Ἰουδαίων ἀκριβῶς, καὶ τί τὸ γένος αὐτοῦ καὶ ὅσα ἐνεδείξατο τῷ ἔθνει αὐτῶν καὶ πῶς ἀπέθανεν σταυρωθείς. Προκομίσαντες γὰρ αὐτοῦ τὰ ὑπομνήματα ἐπανέγνωσάν μοι
_unresolved_facts.fix: disparages Christ as a crucified man, saying he learned from Jews Christ's race/family, what he displayed to their nation, and how he died crucified; for they produced his records and read them back to him

_unresolved_facts.claim: After counsel the governor puts nails under the joints and nails Conon's feet
_unresolved_facts.source_quote: Σκεψάμενος μετὰ τῶν συνέδρων αὐτοῦ κελεύει ἥλους γενέσθαι ὑπὸ ἄρθρων καὶ καθηλώσας τοὺς πόδας τοῦ μάρτυρος
_unresolved_facts.fix: After deliberation with his councilors he orders nails to be made/put under the joints, and having nailed the martyr's feet

_unresolved_facts.claim: City-father devoted to idols who hunts Christians and has Conon bound
_unresolved_facts.source_quote: πατὴρ πόλεως, καὶ ἄλλος τις, νεωκόρος, ἐμμανόμενος καὶ αὐτὸς τῇ ἀσεβείᾳ τῶν εἰδώλων, ἠξίωσαν τὸν ἡγεμόνα δοθῆναι αὐτοῖς βοήθειαν
_unresolved_facts.fix: City-father who, with another person (a neōkoros) raging in the impiety of idols, requested help from the governor to search; later he specifically orders Conon bound to his horse
Origen speaks in section 2 and reports in section 3, but in section 3 the speech is introduced simply with Ὠριγένης λέγει without ὁ Ὠριγένης

_unresolved_facts.source_quote: Λέγει ὁ Ναόδωρος τῷ Ὠριγένει· Ἡ ὁδὸς ἡμῶν οὐ κενὴ ἐγενήθη
_unresolved_facts.fix: Naodorus speaks in sections 2 and 3: in section 2 he speaks to Origen ('Our journey has not been in vain'), and in section 3 he presents Conon to the governor
